type:
∀ {x : ℝ},
  Irrational x →
    (LeanEval.NumberTheory.ThueSiegelRothProblem.IsDiophantine x ↔ ∀ {κ : ℝ}, (Roth.approxSet x κ).Infinite → κ ≤ 2)
what: For an irrational real number, uniform positive lower bounds at every exponent2+epsilon are equivalent to an upper bound2 on all exponents having infinitely many unreduced approximation pairs.
how: Uses Roth.eventually_div_rpow_lt to absorb a positive constant into an epsilon half-gap, removes finitely many bounded-denominator pairs with Roth.approxSet_den_le_finite, and uses the private finite-positive-minimum helper for the reverse implication.
hypotheses: The original has Irrational x; fresh all-real proof derives it from either side and removes that binder. Real powers and positive denominators remain.
caller_summary: One explicit same-file caller thueSiegelRoth at LeanEval:63; zero external-to-file. Complete original inlining and new all-real recovery preserve its exact signature and eliminate target reference.
mathlib_api_audit: LiouvilleWith and its frequently_lt_rpow_neg/affine API are relevant building blocks; no direct uniform-bound/cutoff equivalence hit was verified. The generic bridge is authored proof, not an existing mathlib call.
moral_duplications: Shares exponent-gap and finite-denominator tools with Main.reduction; these serve different statements. Private positive-minimum helper supplies one direction; no duplicate full equivalence found.

generalization.all_real_type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, IsDiophantine x ↔ ∀ {κ : ℝ}, (Roth.approxSet x κ).Infinite → κ ≤ 2
generalization.generic_type: ∀ {t x : ℝ}, UniformBound t x ↔ ∀ {κ : ℝ}, (pairSet x κ).Infinite → κ ≤ t
generalization.modern_type: ∀ {t x : ℝ}, UniformBound t x ↔ Irrational x ∧ ∀ {p : ℝ}, LiouvilleWith p x → p ≤ t
generalization.conditions: No positivity condition on t; Liouville bridge retains irrationality; fixed2 recovered without assumption

missing_api: Generic finite-exception/uniform-bound and exponent-cutoff bridges; decide normal form before exporting new definitions.
junk: Not dead: actual final caller. One caller alone does not turn its nontrivial proof into a mathlib composition.

Should the canonical public bridge use denominator-frequency LiouvilleWith directly, keeping unreduced pairSet and its equivalence in a secondary interface module?
